exhibits.title: The five questions and our answers
exhibits.subtitle: Foreign-invested convenience chain · rules in force from 18 Oct 2026 · confidence = our judgement of the evidence
rows: 1 · Licensing route for the first and each additional store

Investment and enterprise certificates, a retail business licence, then one outlet licence per store from the province; the first store can be filed with the business licence when it sits in the head-office province [Decree 342/2026]
2 · When the needs test applies, and the exemptions

Every convenience store or mini-supermarket after the first, unless the investor is covered by CPTPP, EVFTA or UKVFTA; only non-convenience units under 500 m² inside a mall are exempt by size [Decree 342/2026]
3 · Who decides, on what, how long, at what cost

A provincial council (People's Committee, industry and trade, finance, police) judges the commune market in 20 working days; the full clock is 14-48 working days; each month of waiting costs a store about USD 12,000 [Kira estimates]

Food-safety certificate for cooked food, a commune licence for spirits, no tobacco for foreign-invested retailers, fire-safety duties, cash-register e-invoices, and an outlet licence that ends with the lease
5 · Structure that minimises approval risk, and the triggers

Treaty-country owner: own company. Non-treaty owner: franchise to Vietnamese-owned operators; on our reading a local-majority JV still carries the foreign partner's test. Go if 9 in 10 licences issue within 30 working days
exhibits.source: Source: [Decree 342/2026]; cost of delay [Kira estimates]; detail and sources on the chapter pages

exhibits.title: What would have to be true, and how to test it
exhibits.subtitle: Foreign-invested convenience chain · Vietnam · confidence = our judgement of the evidence at Oct 2026
rows: Outlet licences issue in 14-20 working days for a treaty owner
Track the first 10 files after 18 Oct; go if 9 in 10 issue within 30 working days
Councils approve non-treaty stores without repeated requests
File 3 stores in 2 provinces with a full ward census; count requests for more information
The security review stays a 14-day step
Ask the provincial industry and trade office how it will consult; file the first post-100 licence early
Landlords accept rent-free periods tied to licence issue
Put the clause in the first 20 lease negotiations; go if half accept
Franchisees hold format and food standards
Five-store franchise pilot with monthly audit scores against company stores
The new food law adds no pre-market approval for own-label meals
Follow the amended food-safety law through the late-2026 Assembly session; declare own-label products early
